description.en: Découvrez comment les composants Haystack interagissent avec les LLM, comprenez ce qui distingue les agents des modèles de langue traditionnels et créez votre premier agent fonctionnel. Vous verrez ensuite comment donner à votre agent l’accès à des outils du monde réel, comme la recherche web, pour le transformer d’un simple répondant en véritable résolveur de problèmes actif !

body.fr:
## Avant de commencer

Ce cours se réalise directement dans Neopolis avec des activités interactives. Pour les mises en situation, préparez un chatbot IA autorisé par votre organisation ; ne partagez jamais de données sensibles, de mots de passe ou de clés API.

## Before you start

This course is completed in Neopolis through interactive activities. For the scenarios, prepare an AI chatbot approved by your organization; never share sensitive data, passwords, or API keys.

blocks.transcript:
1. Bienvenue dans le cours !
Hello and welcome to this course on building AI agents using Haystack!

2. Votre formateur·rice
I’m Bilge from deepset, and I’ll be your instructor for this course. In this course, you’ll learn how to build smart AI agents using Haystack. Whether you're new to agents or just new to Haystack, you're in the right place.

3. À propos de l’agent : agent de santé
You won’t just be learning about agents in theory. You’ll actually build one step by step with real components, tools, and data. And this won’t be a generic agent either. You’ll create a healthcare agent that can respond to user queries by combining up-to-date online information with private, structured patient data.

4. À propos de l’agent : agent de santé
Your agent will be able to access the web to fetch current medical insights — like treatment guidelines or drug interactions and query an SQL database that holds patient records: things like age, conditions, and prescribed medications.

5. Votre framework : Haystack
We’ll be using Haystack to build our agent. Haystack is an open-source AI orchestration framework — built for AI engineers, data scientists, and Python developers. It gives us the tools to build real-world, compound, agentic systems that can reason, retrieve, act, and respond like autonomous agents, multi-modal apps, or scalable RAG systems. Haystack is designed to be modular and model-agnostic — meaning we can build our system with our choice of LLMs and tools, without being locked into one provider or platform.

6. Haystack avec des outils
Additionally, in this course, we’ll be using OpenAI as our LLM provider and to let the agent search the web, we’ll connect it to the Google Search API through Serper.

7. Notre démarche de construction
By the end of this course, you’ll not only understand how agents work, but you’ll also have a working prototype that can interpret natural language queries, make smart decisions, and act on them using the right tools at the right time.

8. Passons à la pratique !
Let’s get started. In the next exercise, we’ll start exploring Haystack components by talking to a language model directly. Understanding how to communicate with LLMs is the first step toward building a complete agent.

projectorSlides.title: Que peut faire un agent Haystack ?
projectorSlides.script: Let’s take a moment to understand what an AI agent actually is and what makes it different from just using a large language model on its own.
projectorSlides.instructorTitle: DevRel Engineer for Haystack at deepset

projectorSlides.title: Comparer LLM et agents
projectorSlides.script:
Large language models, on their own, are powerful, but limited. They can answer questions, summarize text, or write code. But they can’t interact with the outside world. They can’t fetch real-time data, query a private database, trigger a function. Once they generate a response, that’s it, they’re done.
That’s where the key difference lies.
An AI agent is an autonomous system that can understand a user’s request, figure out what needs to be done, and take real actions using external tools. It still relies on an LLM to reason and interpret language, but it doesn’t stop at generating a response. It goes beyond that.
projectorSlides.content:
- Un modèle de langage puissant 
- Idéal pour le génératif (répondre, écrire du code) 
- Aucune interaction avec l’extérieur 

- Un système autonome basé sur un LLM 
- Comprend l’intention, planifie et agit en conséquence 
- Accès à des outils pour interagir avec l’extérieur

projectorSlides.script: Agents don’t just generate text; they make decisions.

projectorSlides.title: Atouts des agents
projectorSlides.script:
When they get a question, they think things through, like: 
“Do I need to search the web for up-to-date information?”

projectorSlides.title: Atouts des agents

projectorSlides.title: Atouts des agents

projectorSlides.title: Atouts des agents
projectorSlides.script: And then, they actually take those actions. This kind of behavior is known as function calling or tool use — and it’s what gives agents their real power.
projectorSlides.content: - Function Calling = la force de l’agent
projectorSlides.contentLeft: - Function Calling = la force de l’agent

projectorSlides.script: Creating an agent with Haystack is quite straightforward. We give it a language model to power its thinking,

projectorSlides.script: external APIs,

projectorSlides.script: other Haystack components like retrievers, rankers, or other agents,

projectorSlides.title: Agents dans Haystack
projectorSlides.script: and even connections to MCP servers for distributed tasks. We define the tools, and the agent figures out how to use them based on the situation.

projectorSlides.title: Notre agent santé
projectorSlides.script: In this course, we’ll build a healthcare agent that decides whether to query a patient database, search the web for medical information, or combine both to answer a complex question. The language model handles the reasoning, and Haystack takes care of the orchestration.

Let’s take a moment to understand what an AI agent actually is and what makes it different from just using a large language model on its own.

2. Comparer LLM et agents
Large language models, on their own, are powerful, but limited. They can answer questions, summarize text, or write code. But they can’t interact with the outside world. They can’t fetch real-time data, query a private database, trigger a function. Once they generate a response, that’s it, they’re done.
That’s where the key difference lies.
An AI agent is an autonomous system that can understand a user’s request, figure out what needs to be done, and take real actions using external tools. It still relies on an LLM to reason and interpret language, but it doesn’t stop at generating a response. It goes beyond that.

3. Atouts des agents
Agents don’t just generate text; they make decisions.

4. Atouts des agents
When they get a question, they think things through, like: 
“Do I need to search the web for up-to-date information?”

5. Atouts des agents
“Should I run a function to calculate something?”

6. Atouts des agents
“Is this a case where I should look in a database?”

7. Atouts des agents
And then, they actually take those actions. This kind of behavior is known as function calling or tool use — and it’s what gives agents their real power.

8. Agents dans Haystack
Creating an agent with Haystack is quite straightforward. We give it a language model to power its thinking,

a system prompt to steer its behavior,

and a list of tools it can call. Those tools could be Python functions,

external APIs,

other Haystack components like retrievers, rankers, or other agents,

13. Agents dans Haystack
and even connections to MCP servers for distributed tasks. We define the tools, and the agent figures out how to use them based on the situation.

14. Notre agent santé
In this course, we’ll build a healthcare agent that decides whether to query a patient database, search the web for medical information, or combine both to answer a complex question. The language model handles the reasoning, and Haystack takes care of the orchestration.

15. Passons à la pratique !
Let’s start creating our agent.

description.en: Dans ce chapitre, dotez vos agents d’outils pour les rendre plus intelligents, plus transparents et plus faciles à déboguer. Du traçage des décisions de l’agent avec des callbacks en streaming à la création de pipelines Haystack réutilisables, vous ferez évoluer vos agents vers un large éventail de capacités, y compris l’exécution de requêtes SQL. Préparez-vous à personnaliser, connecter et booster votre pipeline Haystack !

projectorSlides.title: Ouvrir la boîte noire : rendre les agents transparents
projectorSlides.script: We now have a fully working agent, one that can choose tools and pull in real-world data to answer a user’s question.
projectorSlides.instructorTitle: DevRel Engineer for Haystack at deepset

projectorSlides.title: Des LLM aux agents
projectorSlides.script:
But if we take a closer look at the agent we’ve built so far, we’ll notice a big gap: we can’t actually see what’s happening inside the agent when it generates a response.
The lack of visibility is a real problem — especially when we're trying to build a reliable system such as our healthcare agent. 

Let’s say we asked the agent a question and it gave us a helpful response.
projectorSlides.content: - Peut interagir ✅   Impossible de voir l’intérieur ❌
projectorSlides.contentLeft: - Peut interagir ✅   Impossible de voir l’intérieur ❌

projectorSlides.title: Manque de visibilité
projectorSlides.script: But we have no idea if that answer was based on a tool call or just the model making something up. There’s no way to tell whether it actually used the search tool we gave it or hallucinated an answer instead.

projectorSlides.title: Manque de visibilité
projectorSlides.script: This makes it really difficult to evaluate the correctness of the response, especially in cases where accuracy and trustworthiness are critical.

projectorSlides.title: Débogage
projectorSlides.script: Another major challenge is debugging. If the agent gives an incorrect answer, what exactly went wrong? Was the wrong tool used? Was the right tool used with the wrong parameters? Or did the tool return something useful but the model just ignored it? Right now, with the default agent behavior, we don’t know. We’re flying blind.
projectorSlides.content: - Mauvais usage d’outil, mauvais paramètres, hallucination
projectorSlides.contentLeft: - Mauvais usage d’outil, mauvais paramètres, hallucination

projectorSlides.title: Agents transparents
projectorSlides.script: To build robust, testable, and trustworthy agents, we need transparency.

projectorSlides.title: Agents transparents
projectorSlides.script: We need to see when the agent decides to use a tool, the input it sends, the output it gets back

projectorSlides.title: Agents transparents
projectorSlides.script:
and how that result influences the final answer. This is what turns agent development from guesswork into an engineering process.
In the next exercise, we’ll address this head-on. We’ll customize our agent to trace tool usage and inspect intermediate steps in real time during development. This kind of tracing is essential when we’re building and debugging our agent.

projectorSlides.script: Let’s take a look.

projectorSlides.title: Bilan et prochaines étapes
projectorSlides.script: Congrats on making it to the end of this course!
projectorSlides.instructorTitle: DevRel Engineer for Haystack at deepset

projectorSlides.title: Vous avez créé un agent réel avec Haystack !
projectorSlides.script: You’ve just completed a hands-on journey into building AI agents using Haystack. You’ve learned how to create systems that don’t just generate responses but reason, interact with external data sources, and make decisions.

projectorSlides.title: Agents capables de raisonner et d’agir
projectorSlides.script: At the beginning, we interacted directly with a language model. It could generate text, but it had no awareness of the world or tools to act with.

projectorSlides.title: Agents capables de raisonner et d’agir
projectorSlides.script:
Then, we built our first agent by giving it access to tools, starting with real-time web search, and later, structured patient records in an SQL database. 
Along the way, we learned how to use Haystack to build an AI agent in just couple of steps.

projectorSlides.title: Agents capables de raisonner et d’agir
projectorSlides.script: First, we integrated the SerperDevWebSearch component as the agent’s first tool, giving it access to real-time web information. We then improved the agent’s transparency and traceability through custom configurations.

projectorSlides.title: Agents capables de raisonner et d’agir
projectorSlides.script: Next, we built a text-to-SQL pipeline that converted natural language questions into SQL queries, executed them on a patient database, and returned the results. Finally, we wrapped that pipeline as a tool and connected it back to the agent. That’s how we combined dynamic reasoning with structured workflows, all within a unified system.

projectorSlides.title: Prochaines étapes
projectorSlides.script:
If you want to explore further, you can level up by building multi-agent systems, adding multimodal capabilities like image or PDF support, and deploying your agents in production with Hayhooks.
Agents are one of the most exciting frontiers in AI, and you now have the skills to help shape what comes next.

projectorSlides.title: Passons à la pratique !
projectorSlides.script: Thanks for joining me on this journey, happy building!
